claims: Artemis II mission launched on April 1, 2026.
Artemis II mission is a 10-day crewed flight.
Artemis II mission tests the Orion spacecraft.
Artemis II mission tests the SLS rocket.
Artemis II mission involves flight around the Moon.
Astronauts on Artemis II mission are Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
Artemis II mission marks the first human deep-space mission in over 50 years.
Space Launch System (SLS) lifted off from Kennedy Space Center's Launch Complex 39B at 6:35 p.m. EDT on April 1, 2026.
SLS successfully inserted the Orion spacecraft into Earth orbit.
On Day 1 of Artemis II mission, following separation, the crew spent 90 minutes in a high Earth elliptical orbit.
On Day 1 of Artemis II mission, the crew tested life support systems.
On Day 1 of Artemis II mission, the crew deployed solar arrays.
On Day 2 of Artemis II mission, Interim Cryogenic Propulsion Stage (ICPS) fires.
Interim Cryogenic Propulsion Stage (ICPS) boosts the crew from Earth orbit onto a figure-eight trajectory toward the Moon.
Days 2-4 of Artemis II mission involve outbound transit to the Moon.
During days 2-4 of Artemis II mission, the crew refines the spacecraft's systems.
On Day 5 of Artemis II mission, Orion enters the Moon’s sphere of influence.
On Day 5 of Artemis II mission, Orion begins swing around the far side of the Moon.
On Day 6 of Artemis II mission, the crew flies to the far side of the Moon.
On Day 6 of Artemis II mission, the crew momentarily loses contact with Earth.
On Day 6 of Artemis II mission, the crew performs manual close-proximity flight maneuvers.
On Day 6 of Artemis II mission, the crew takes images of the lunar surface.
Days 7-9 of Artemis II mission are return trip to Earth.
On Day 10 of Artemis II mission, the crew module separates from the service module.
On Day 10 of Artemis II mission, the crew module performs high-speed high-heat re-entry through Earth’s atmosphere.
On Day 10 of Artemis II mission, the crew module splashes down in the Pacific Ocean.
Backup launch windows for Artemis II mission were available on April 2-6, 2026, and April 30, 2026.
Backup launch opportunities for Artemis II mission were at Adler Planetarium.
